title: Landfall and Compass
premise: Juniper Winterbourne has spent a decade piloting cargo up the Vell River, outrunning debts, memories, and the family name he abandoned. When a flood unearths a chest bearing the seal of Ostrava—a nation erased from every map forty years ago—its contents name him heir to a claim that could restore the drowned kingdom or destroy the coalition that buried it. Hunted by coalition agents and shadowed by Sera Quill, an archivist who believes the chest holds proof her own family was erased with it, Juniper must pilot his aging boat past checkpoints, rapids, and old betrayals to the river's forbidden source, where the truth of Ostrava's fall—and of his father's role in it—waits in a flooded archive. As the monsoon makes landfall and the river turns against them, Juniper must choose between surrendering the claim to save Sera's life or holding it and becoming the man who stops running, ending with him giving up the throne he never wanted but claiming, at last, a name and a home.
about_author: Ansel Ravensworth is the pen name of a former barge-hand turned novelist who spent six years working the inland waterways of three continents before trading the wheelhouse for a writing desk. His fiction is known for its river-haunted prose and characters who mistake motion for freedom.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Juniper pilots the Marguerite through a fog-bound bend, reading water like scripture while refusing a lucrative contract that would anchor him in one port. POV: Juniper. Beat: restless competence masking avoidance—he knows stopping costs more than moving.

chapters.title: What the Flood Gives Back
chapters.summary: After a night storm, Juniper's deckhand hauls aboard a waterlogged chest stamped with Ostrava's triple-crown seal; inside are documents naming 'J. Winterbourne' as lawful heir. POV: Juniper. Beat: dread dressed as curiosity—the past has found him whether he likes it or not.

chapters.title: A Nation With No Address
chapters.summary: In a riverside tavern, Juniper learns Ostrava was dissolved by treaty after a coup; mentioning it is now sedition. A stranger photographs the chest and vanishes. POV: Juniper. Beat: the scale of danger becomes real—this isn't salvage, it's a fuse.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Sera Quill boards at Casterly Wharf claiming to be a coal surveyor; by dawn Juniper catches her copying the documents. She confesses: her family was among those erased when Ostrava fell. POV: Sera. Beat: wary alliance—two people using each other as shields.

chapters.title: Coal Dust and Gunmetal
chapters.summary: Coalition agents board under customs pretense; Juniper hides the chest in the boiler flue and lies with a captain's calm, but Agent Brannic marks him. POV: Juniper. Beat: first bloodless skirmish—his talent for evasion now has a witness.

chapters.title: The Contract He Refused
chapters.summary: The refused contract resurfaces: its backer is Lord Aldous Vane, the treaty's architect, offering Juniper wealth to hand over the chest—or ruin if he won't. POV: Sera. Beat: temptation with teeth; duty and survival pull opposite ways.

chapters.title: Night Run Through the Narrows
chapters.summary: Fleeing Vane's patrol boat, Juniper takes the Marguerite through unnavigable narrows at night, nearly losing the hull and his nerve. POV: Juniper. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear—he can outrun anything except what's inside the chest.

chapters.title: The Father in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Sera deciphers the documents: Juniper's father signed the dissolution treaty, then secretly preserved the royal registry—meaning Juniper inherits both the crown's claim and the traitor's guilt. POV: Sera. Beat: identity shatters; the name he fled was never the one he thought.

chapters.title: Port of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Grounded for repairs, Juniper and Sera grow close in a dockside week of shared work and stories; he almost tells her why he keeps moving. POV: alternating. Beat: love arrives quietly, exactly where he swore not to stand still.

chapters.title: Brannic's Net
chapters.summary: Brannic arrests the deckhand and offers a trade: the chest for the boy. Juniper pays with his savings instead, learning Vane wants more than paper—he wants the source archive destroyed. POV: Juniper. Beat: the cost of caring about people, itemized.

chapters.title: The Map Beneath the Map
chapters.summary: The registry reveals a second cache at the river's source—a flooded archive holding proof of who really ordered Ostrava's massacre. The route is forbidden, charted only in fragments. POV: Sera. Beat: purpose crystallizes; the journey gains a destination worth dying for.

chapters.title: Passage Bought in Lies
chapters.summary: To pass the checkpoint at Grey Locks, Juniper poses as a Vane contractor, using forged papers Sera prepared; the deception works but burns their last safe identity. POV: Juniper. Beat: he becomes fluent in the lying his father once mastered.

chapters.title: Rapids Called the Judgment
chapters.summary: The Marguerite tears her paddlewheel in the Judgment Rapids; stranded, the crew mutinies until Juniper's honesty about the danger wins them back. POV: crew member Tull. Beat: leadership redefined—not evasion now, but standing in front of people.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Vane intercepts them with gunboats and makes his real offer: legitimacy, a pardon, and Sera's safety—if Juniper surrenders the claim and lets the archive drown. POV: Juniper. Beat: love against duty made literal; he refuses and hates how much he wants to say yes.

chapters.title: The Long Climb
chapters.summary: Above the last navigable mile, they abandon ship and haul the chest overland toward the source gorge as monsoon clouds stack black on the horizon. POV: Sera. Beat: exhaustion and resolve; the river that carried them now bars the way.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weir
chapters.summary: Tull, bought by Brannic, steals the chest and the maps; Juniper catches him at the weir, and in the struggle the boy falls. Juniper saves him, and Tull confesses everything. POV: Juniper. Beat: mercy as a weapon—he chooses the man he'll be over the advantage.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: The monsoon hits early; rain like nails, the gorge flooding. They shelter in a cliff cave where Sera finds carvings proving her family served the crown faithfully—her erasure was personal, ordered by Vane himself. POV: Sera. Beat: grief transmuted into fury and clarity.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: At the source, behind a waterfall swollen by the storm, they enter the flooded vault; diving in rising water, Juniper recovers the massacre order bearing Vane's signature and his father's counter-seal. POV: Juniper. Beat: climax begins—the whole inheritance in one waterproof case.

chapters.title: Stand at the Source
chapters.summary: Vane's men arrive; in the collapsing vault, Juniper stands his ground for the first time in his life, buying Sera time to secure the documents as the water rises. POV: Juniper. Beat: the runner stops running; courage costs him the escape route.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: The vault floods fully; Brannic, seeing Vane's signature, switches sides and lets them live, taking the evidence to the tribunal instead. Vane's power cracks. POV: Brannic. Beat: the antagonist's machine turns on itself; truth outswims violence.

chapters.title: The Claim Renounced
chapters.summary: Before the tribunal at Casterly Wharf, Juniper publicly renounces the crown but presents the evidence, restoring citizenship and names to Ostrava's scattered survivors—including Sera's family. POV: Sera. Beat: inheritance fulfilled by refusal; he claims the name by giving away the throne.

chapters.title: Compass
chapters.summary: Spring again: the repaired Marguerite runs cargo on the Vell, Juniper at the wheel with Sera beside him and a home port he no longer flees. The river still changes its moods; so does he. POV: Juniper. Beat: resolution—stopping no longer costs more than staying, because he finally knows whose man he is.
